entry.title: [Metalama.Framework] Metalama allows local code execution through DLL planting in shared temporary directories
entry.content:
Summary

Metalama loaded and executed compile-time assemblies, auxiliary executable tools, and embedded helper assemblies from predictable temporary directories. On Linux and macOS the default cache location was the world-writable system temporary directory (Path.GetTempPath(), i.e. /tmp), and previously-generated artifacts were trusted based on the presence of a sentinel/.completed marker file rather than on any integrity verification.

A local, unprivileged user on a shared machine or CI/build agent can pre-create the deterministic cache directory structure and plant a malicious DLL together with the matching sentinel file. When a higher-privileged user (or build/service account) subsequently runs a build, Metalama finds the sentinel, skips regeneration, and loads and executes the attacker-supplied assembly inside the compiler / IDE / MSBuild process.

Affected load-and-execute paths:

  • the cache of compile-time assemblies that Metalama generates from your aspects;
  • auxiliary executable tools that Metalama extracts to a local directory and then launches;
  • embedded .NET helper assemblies that Metalama extracts to a local directory and loads into the build / IDE process.

Impact

Arbitrary code execution in the security context of the building user — i.e. a local privilege escalation across user accounts on shared POSIX systems (multi-user developer machines, CI/build agents). The attacker obtains code execution as the victim without holding the victim's privileges, and can read source/secrets, tamper with build output (supply-chain injection), or disrupt builds.

Affected configurations

  • Linux and macOS, default configuration — affected. The shipped default uses the world-writable system temp directory.
  • Windows, default configuration — not affected. The default per-user temporary directory is protected by OS ACLs, so cross-user planting is not possible.
  • The METALAMA_TEMP environment variable is a deployer-controlled override and is out of scope: pointing it at an insecure (e.g. world-writable or attacker-owned) location is a deployment misconfiguration, not a defect in the product.

Severity

CVSS v3.1: AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H = 8.2 (High) for the affected POSIX default configuration (Scope:Changed reflects the cross-user privilege escalation).

CVSS v4.0 cross-check: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:L/VI:H/VA:L/SC:L/SI:H/SA:H = 6.0 (Medium), which more granularly attributes low impact to the cache itself and high impact to the subsequent build process. The honest range is therefore Medium-High depending on the scoring model and platform.

Fix

Caches and extraction directories were relocated from the world-writable system temp directory to per-user application-data locations ($XDG_CACHE_HOME / ~/.cache/Metalama on POSIX), relying on OS-enforced per-user ownership as the trust boundary. Fixed in 2026.1.19.

Weaknesses

  • CWE-377: Insecure Temporary File
  • CWE-427: Uncontrolled Search Path Element

Affected packages

  • Metalama.Framework < 2026.1.19,
  • Metalama.Tool < 2026.1.19

Internal tracking: metalama/Metalama#1650.

entry.title: [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86] Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70035 - .NET and Visual Studio Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
entry.content:
Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

Restrictive XAML and XPS security fixes block unsafe URI fetching and navigation, propagate untrusted-input state through hyperlink navigation, add TrueType font protection and XAML nesting-depth limits, and avoid caching positive DNS zone-policy decisions.

Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/451

CVSS Details

  • Version: 3.1

  • Severity: High

  • Score: 8.8

  • Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

  • Weakness: CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)

Affected Platforms

  • Platforms: Windows
  • Architectures: All

Affected Packages

The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below.

Package name Affected version Patched version
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64 >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 10.0.13
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64 >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 10.0.13
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86 >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 10.0.13
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64 >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 8.0.32
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64 >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 8.0.32
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86 >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 8.0.32
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64 >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 9.0.21
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64 >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 9.0.21
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86 >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 9.0.21
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64 >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 11.0.0-rc.2
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64 >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 11.0.0-rc.2
Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86 >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 11.0.0-rc.2

Advisory FAQ

How do I know if I am affected?

If using a package listed in affected packages, you're exposed to the vulnerability.

How do I fix the issue?

  1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs.
  2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the dotnet --info command.

Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect.

Additionally, if you've deployed self-contained applications targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed.

The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.

entry.title: [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64] Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70186 - ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability
entry.content:
Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock Kestrel connection handling. Repeated requests can cause excessive blocked-thread creation and exhaust server resources, resulting in denial of service.

Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461

  • Version: 3.1

  • Severity: High

  • Score: 7.5

  • Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

  • Weakness: CWE-833 (Deadlock)

Affected Platforms

  • Platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS with HTTP/3 support
  • Architectures: All
